AITA for telling a co-worker's boss that she posted on Facebook that she "told her bosses she was quitting but they didn't accept it"? Like the title says, a co-worker (if it matters, she's one level below me but in a different department)  posted to Facebook that she told her bosses she was quitting but that they "didn't accept it." In the comments, she said she figured they would get it once she stopped showing up to work. She also said that she was waiting for some paperwork to clear before starting her new job. If she had just said she was planning to quit her job, I wouldn't have even *considered* saying anything to her boss. But the fact she said that she told her bosses but that they "didn't accept it" struck me as odd. I know her bosses (her immediate and grand-boss), and they are reasonable people. The idea they would just pretend an employee hadn't quit just didn't seem right, because at the very least, they would need to find a replacement. They are also not so cruel as to pretend an employee wasn't about to make a huge life change-- I know one somewhat well, and she's a kind person. Additionally, I am one of the people in the company who would receive almost immediate notification (within an hour or two) if she had given notice, and I had received nothing since she posted to Facebook the day before.

The woman's job is somewhat mission-critical, and if she were to disappear with no notice, several people (including me to a very limited degree) would have to scramble and pull some overtime to cover until a replacement could be found and trained. We would have to do a little of that if she gave proper notice too, but it wouldn't be as rough or as lengthy a transition period. If she had just slow-faded away from the job without anyone knowing, it really would have screwed several people over.

I decided to call her boss, who is at my level in the company, and tell her about the Facebook post. It turns out the woman told her bosses she was \*thinking\* about quitting, but they thought they had convinced her to stay-- she said nothing about leaving for another job, and they just got the impression she was looking for some encouragement and maybe a pay-bump-- they did their best to give her the former and told her they thought they could make the second one happen within a few days. Apparently, the woman called in sick today. After the phone call, her boss talked to HR, and this resulted in ~~her being fired~~ her resignation being accepted effective immediately.

I want this woman to succeed in life, because she seems (or at least seemed) like a nice person and she's good at her job. But I still feel guilty and like I did something wrong.

Edits: HR called to fill me in. She wasn't fired. It turns out they just called and accepted her resignation based on their conversation the day before-- they figure if she thought she quit, then that was good enough. Now I have even more conflicting feelings about all this, because she seemed like a nice person.
